---
title: Lore
kind: service
visibility: internal
status: active
summary: Durable agent memory, long-lived notes, and consolidated handoff context.
tags: [memory, notes, recall]
---

# Lore

Lore keeps durable agent memory, long-lived notes, and consolidated session captures for Hermes handoffs.

It works beside [[services/flow]] for work-state and links to [[runbooks/retrieval-triage]] and [[projects/agent-memory-first]].

---
title: Flow
kind: service
visibility: internal
status: active
summary: Agent-first work queue with review lanes, auto-claim, and durable notes.
tags: [board, queue, review]
---

# Flow

Flow is the agent-first work queue and review board.

It auto-claims todo work on start, keeps review-lane audit trails, and expects verification notes with commit SHAs.

See [[services/lore]] for durable memory and [[runbooks/retrieval-triage]] for the nightly review routine.

---
title: Hermes
kind: service
visibility: internal
status: active
summary: Session recap agent that bridges handoffs into Lore and follow-up work into Flow.
tags: [handoff, recap, agent]
---

# Hermes

Hermes writes session recaps, pushes durable handoff context into [[services/lore]], and opens follow-up work in [[services/flow]].

The broader roadmap lives in [[projects/agent-memory-first]].

---
title: Muse
kind: service
visibility: internal
status: active
summary: Inference service that now routes generation through a vLLM gateway.
tags: [inference, gateway, runtime]
---

# Muse

Muse now routes inference through a vLLM gateway for Hermes and Atlas workloads.

The retrieval and memory roadmap is tracked in [[projects/agent-memory-first]].

---
title: Atlas API
kind: service
visibility: internal
status: active
summary: Atlas API now deploys on Fly.io with post-migration smoke checks.
tags: [deploy, flyio, api]
---

# Atlas API

Atlas API now deploys on Fly.io after the Render migration.

Rollback and smoke-test expectations are captured in [[decisions/deploy-policy]], and Atlas uses [[services/muse]] for inference.

---
title: Agent Memory First
kind: project
visibility: internal
status: active
summary: Roadmap for durable memory, retrieval policy, and session handoff quality.
tags: [roadmap, memory, retrieval]
---

# Agent Memory First

The project ties together [[services/lore]], [[services/hermes]], and [[services/muse]].

It follows [[decisions/retrieval-policy]] and treats nightly validation in [[runbooks/retrieval-triage]] as the guardrail for recall quality.

---
title: Retrieval Policy
kind: decision
visibility: internal
status: accepted
summary: Retrieval should use term fallback, graph expansion, and prefer the latest live claim after updates.
tags: [retrieval, graph, contradiction]
---

# Retrieval Policy

Retrieval should add term fallback when exact phrases miss, expand through the context graph for linked pages, and prefer the latest live claim after contradiction updates.

This decision supports [[projects/agent-memory-first]] and the nightly checks in [[runbooks/retrieval-triage]].

---
title: Retrieval Triage
kind: runbook
visibility: internal
status: active
summary: Nightly checklist for paraphrase misses, contradiction updates, and recall regressions.
tags: [runbook, paraphrase, triage]
---

# Retrieval Triage

Use this nightly checklist for paraphrase misses, contradiction updates, and recall regressions.

It points to [[decisions/retrieval-policy]], checks the handoff stack in [[services/lore]], and records follow-up work in [[services/flow]].

---
title: Archive Worker
kind: service
visibility: internal
status: active
summary: Background worker that compacts nightly raw notes and stale session artifacts.
tags: [archive, cleanup, notes]
---

# Archive Worker

Archive Worker compacts nightly raw notes and stale session artifacts.

It is intentionally separate from [[services/lore]] and does not own durable recall quality.

---
title: Deploy Policy
kind: decision
visibility: internal
status: accepted
summary: Atlas migrations require smoke checks, rollback hooks, and verification notes.
tags: [deploy, rollback, smoke]
---

# Deploy Policy

Atlas migrations require smoke checks, rollback hooks, and verification notes.

The current hosting target is [[services/atlas-api]], and inference dependencies flow through [[services/muse]].

---
title: RRF Sentinel
kind: service
visibility: internal
status: active
summary: Lexical anchor for hybrid fusion and loose multi-word retrieval.
tags: [uniqueprefixanchor, lexical, fusion]
---

# RRF Sentinel

The memory subsystem keeps several unrelated operational words between the opening term and the gateway boundary.

The uniqueprefixanchor identifier exists only to guard FTS prefix recall when sparse vector token matching has no exact query token.

---
title: Expansion Anchor
kind: note
visibility: internal
status: active
summary: Direct lexical seed for the graph-only retrieval sentinel.
tags: [expansionseedomega]
---

# Expansion Anchor

The expansionseedomega probe points only to [[services/graph-only-target]].

---
title: Sealed Context Target
kind: service
visibility: internal
status: active
summary: Opaque destination used to prove linked context traversal.
tags: [sealed, context]
---

# Sealed Context Target

This deliberately opaque destination contains no lexical form of its retrieval probe.

---
title: Ops Lane Sentinel
kind: note
visibility: internal
status: active
lane: ops
summary: Lane-scoped retrieval sentinel for ops-only memory.
tags: [laneopsbeacon, ops]
---

# Ops Lane Sentinel

The laneopsbeacon sentinel belongs only to the ops lane and should not leak into project-scoped retrieval.

---
title: Tenant B Sentinel
kind: note
visibility: internal
status: active
actor: agent:tenant-b
summary: Actor-scoped retrieval sentinel for tenant B.
tags: [tenantbravokey, tenant]
---

# Tenant B Sentinel

The tenantbravokey sentinel belongs only to agent:tenant-b and should stay hidden from other actor scopes.

supersessions.reason: Muse switched from llama.cpp to the vLLM gateway.
Atlas API migrated from Render to Fly.io.

hybrid_queries.expectation: The handoff wording should surface Lore and Hermes in the top 3 even though the query does not use the canonical page titles.

hybrid_queries.query: autonomous work queue with review lanes
hybrid_queries.expectation: Flow should rank in the top 3 for the board paraphrase rather than losing to unrelated note pages.
The runbook should appear through graph expansion from capture notes and show a relevance path in the expanded response.
The retrieval policy decision should be recoverable from the roadmap and debug captures with an explicit graph path.

hybrid_queries.query: bridge session recaps into durable memory and board
hybrid_queries.expectation: Hermes, Lore, and Flow should all be represented in the top 3 for the cross-service handoff workflow.
The latest Muse page should stay in the top 3 after the runtime update instead of drifting behind stale runtime captures.

hybrid_queries.query: where atlas api runs after migration
hybrid_queries.expectation: Atlas API and its deploy policy should stay visible after the Render -> Fly.io update.
The review-lane audit wording should retrieve Flow plus the runbook that tracks the nightly validation work.
The archive distractor control should still resolve to Archive Worker instead of Lore.

hybrid_queries.query: durable memory roadmap for recall quality
hybrid_queries.expectation: The project, Lore, and the retrieval policy should cluster together for the memory roadmap query.

hybrid_queries.query: latest live claim after contradiction update
hybrid_queries.expectation: The contradiction-update guidance should surface the decision and runbook pages through expanded context.
The opaque target has no query terms and must enter the top 3 solely through its link from the lexical anchor.
The FTS prefix-only sentinel must survive hybrid fusion even though sparse vector search has no exact token match.
A loose multi-word prefix query must match the sentinel even though lexical and boundary are not adjacent in its text.
A completely unrelated query should abstain instead of returning arbitrary pages.
The ops-only sentinel should be retrievable when the request is scoped to the ops lane.
The ops-only sentinel must stay out of project-scoped retrieval.
The tenant-B sentinel should be retrievable only when the matching actor scope is requested.
The tenant-B sentinel must stay hidden from other actor scopes.

recall_queries.query: where do handoffs keep long-term notes
recall_queries.expectation: Lore should recall the durable-notes claim, with the Hermes handoff claim also considered relevant.

recall_queries.query: which board auto claims todo work
recall_queries.expectation: Flow should answer both the auto-claim behavior and the board identity.

recall_queries.query: what runtime does Muse use now
recall_queries.expectation: The post-update vLLM claim should rank, and the superseded llama.cpp claim should stay out of the top 3.

recall_queries.query: where does Atlas API deploy now
recall_queries.expectation: The Fly.io claim should rank, and the superseded Render claim should stay out of the top 3.

recall_queries.query: what policy handles phrase only retrieval misses
recall_queries.expectation: The retrieval policy and the roadmap-policy linkage should both count as relevant support.

recall_queries.query: which runbook checks paraphrase misses every night
recall_queries.expectation: The nightly triage runbook claim should rank near the top for the paraphrased checklist query.

recall_queries.query: what bridges session recaps into memory and board work
recall_queries.expectation: The Hermes bridge claims should survive the cross-service recall wording.

recall_queries.query: what keeps the review lane audit trail with sha verification
recall_queries.expectation: The Flow audit-trail claim and the SHA-verification note claim should both be relevant.
The archive distractor control should return Archive Worker rather than Lore memory claims.

recall_queries.query: what does Lore do with session captures
recall_queries.expectation: Lore should recall both the durable-notes and capture-consolidation facts.

recall_queries.query: what should happen after a contradiction update
recall_queries.expectation: The recall policy should explicitly prefer the latest live claim after a contradiction update.
A completely unrelated recall query should abstain instead of returning arbitrary strong claims.
The ops-only claim should be recallable when the request is scoped to the ops lane.
The ops-only claim must stay out of project-scoped recall.
The tenant-B claim should be recallable only when the matching actor scope is requested.
The tenant-B claim must stay hidden from other actor scopes.
The newer matching audit-slot claim should outrank the older equal-strength claim.
